attributes.context: The chunk begins with a definition of technological change as a change in equipment, especially electronic or mechanized, that may reduce bargaining unit employees, reduce work hours, or alter skill requirements; Section 2 states that the parties recognize job displacement and working conditions may be adversely affected by new technology.
The section is titled “HUMAN RESOURCES INFORMATION SYSTEM,” indicating the letter addresses implementation of an HRIS system.

extraction_text: The following Letter of Agreement consolidates the Letters of Agreement between the parties dated 5/13/98 and 6/25/98 regarding implementation of the HRIS system into a single Letter of Agreement and deletes obsolete language.

attributes.context: The provision is part of a letter of agreement addressing a mass transition to a 16th-through-15th pay period, with related notices, optional draw pay, and payroll adjustments.

extraction_text: Universities which change employees from a  $1^{st}$ through  $31^{st}$ pay period to a  $16^{th}$ through  $15^{th}$ pay period, whether voluntarily or involuntarily, will pay the out-of-pocket expenses which employees would normally pay for health insurance during the transition month. It is understood that the “pick up” of health insurance costs is a one-time benefit offered only during the month in which the university makes a mass transition of employees to the  $16^{th}$ through  $15^{th}$ pay period to accommodate the implementation of HRIS.

attributes.context: Article 59, Section 1 defines technological change as a change in equipment of an electronic or mechanized nature that may reduce bargaining unit employees, work hours, or skill requirements; Section 2 states the parties recognize that new technology may adversely affect job displacement, occupational shifts, and working conditions.

extraction_text: (A) The university agrees to give the Union sufficient advance notice of anticipated technological changes which will have a substantial impact on the manner in which job duties of a significant number of employees are performed so that it can review such changes and evaluate the impact on bargaining unit members. With this notice, the university shall inform the Union of whether and to what extent it anticipates that the changes will displace employees, cause a reduction in work hours, cause a change in skill requirements or result in the fragmentation of existing jobs.

attributes.context: Article 59 addresses Technological Change/Retraining; Section 1 defines technological change, and Section 2(A) requires advance notice of anticipated technological changes that substantially affect job duties.

extraction_text: (B) An ad hoc Union/Management Technological Change Committee, composed of three (3) persons from the Union and three (3) persons from management, shall be established for the purposes of reviewing the technological change and its impact on the working conditions of bargaining unit members.

attributes.context: Article 59, Section 2 establishes a Technological Change Committee under Section 2(B); Section 1 defines technological change, and Section 2 recognizes that new technology may adversely affect jobs and working conditions.

extraction_text: (C) The university agrees to meet with the Union to discuss the Committee’s findings and recommendations and it agrees to make every good faith effort to reduce the detrimental effects of technological change on bargaining unit members.

attributes.context: Article 59, Section 2(D) provides that if a regular status employee becomes displaced, the university shall offer retraining under sub (1) or placement under sub (2); Section 1 defines technological change and Section 2 recognizes displacement from new technology.

extraction_text: (2) Should a regular status employee become displaced as a result of technological change, the university shall make a reasonable effort to place the affected employee into another position in the university or other universities within OUS.
